messages:
sam_s: POC with Orion Health — they're seeing SSE streaming disconnects and partial JSON chunks that break their client parser. Intermittent (~10% of streams). Anyone seen this with hosted SSE? request id: req_0a1b2c3d

elaine_dev: can you paste the client's error + a raw stream capture? also are they behind a proxy/Cloudflare/ALB? those often buffer. :thinking:

maria_orion: console error: "SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input". fetch handler shows 200 then connection close mid-payload. using eventsource polyfill in React Native. sample chunk we see: 

    chunk: '{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello' ... (truncated)

support-bot: logs for req_0a1b2c3d: upstream response closed (499) after 3.4s; bytes_sent: 412; model: gpt-4o-mini; region: us-west-2

ryan_infra: 499 = client closed. often client gives up when initial bytes are slow. intermediate proxies may buffer until a threshold then flush or close. two quick repro steps:
1) curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" <url> to see raw SSE
2) confirm the client accumulates until a full SSE event (dont try to parse partial chunk as JSON)

example:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams
```

elaine_dev: also ask them to try disabling gzip (Accept-Encoding: identity) — some CDNs buffer compressed chunks and then flush which can look like big truncated jumps. RN polyfills sometimes hit parser timeouts too.

maria_orion: we're behind FastEdge (edge proxy). curl shows our server sends keepalive comments but the edge strips them. our client times out after 6s and closes. any server-side knobs on hosted API?

sam_s: we can try enabling more frequent keepalives for the tenant or route the POC to a dedicated pool to avoid some edge buffering. ry, is per-tenant heartbeat possible for debugging?

ryan_infra: yes — we can enable an experimental short-heartbeat for that request/tenant for debugging. also recommend either increasing client timeout or use NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) as a fallback; NDJSON is easier for fragile clients. i'll enable heartbeat for req_0a1b2c3d and check FastEdge buffering config.

elaine_dev: if client change is hard, we can ship a small RN parser snippet that accumulates event data until a full JSON object is received. example sketch:
```js
let buf = ''
source.onmessage = (e) => { buf += e.data; try { const obj = JSON.parse(buf); handle(obj); buf = ''; } catch(e) { /* wait for next chunk */ } }
```

support-bot: heartbeat enabled for req_0a1b2c3d at 1779256920. keepalive interval set to 2s for next 24h. note: this is experimental and only for debugging window.

maria_orion: trying again now...

maria_orion: still saw one disconnect after 11s but parser handled partial chunk now. looks much better, thanks. i'll run the POC for 24h and collect failures.

sam_s: next steps:
- ryan_infra: confirm if FastEdge is buffering and share any proxy config changes (proxy_buffering off / X-Accel-Buffering: no / disable gzip where possible)
- elaine_dev: provide NDJSON envelope example + RN parser snippet (short diff)
- maria_orion: validate POC for 24h and post top failure logs with timestamps

can we do a quick screenshare 9am PST tomorrow to watch a repro? @maria_orion

maria_orion: yes 9am PST works.

sam_s: awesome — i'll open a follow-up with meeting link and include a minimal curl reproduction for the customer to run. :thumbsup:

(thumbs-up reactions across thread)
